name: Swiss Ball Leg Curl
description: The Swiss ball leg curl is a bodyweight hamstring exercise performed with the heels resting on a stability ball. The lifter begins in a supine bridge position, then curls the ball toward the hips using knee flexion while maintaining a hip bridge. The instability of the ball increases glute and core activation compared to a lying machine curl. It is an accessible exercise requiring no gym equipment beyond a stability ball.

execution.starting_position: Lie on your back. Place both heels on a Swiss ball with legs extended. Arms by sides or slightly out for stability.
execution.setup_instructions: Inflate the Swiss ball to firm. Place it on a non-slip surface. Lie supine with heels on the ball.
steps: Step 1: Drive the hips up into a bridge position, body forming a straight line from shoulders to heels.
Step 2: While maintaining the hip bridge, curl the ball toward your hips by bending the knees.
Step 3: Pull the ball until the knees are at approximately 90 degrees.
Step 4: Extend the knees to roll the ball back out, maintaining the hip bridge throughout.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the curl, inhale on the extension.
common_mistakes: Hips dropping during the curl, losing the bridge position
Ball rolling to one side due to uneven foot pressure
safety_considerations: Ensure the ball is on a non-slip surface
Keep the core braced throughout to protect the lumbar spine
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full leg extension at the start, curl to 90 degrees or more of knee flexion.
coaching_cues: Curl the ball with your heels
